IdempotencyKeyHeader.description: Opaque key that makes a send safe to retry. A mass send can take longer than the request timeout, and the campaign is already committed by then, so retrying without a key can deliver the broadcast twice. Reuse the same key on a retry: the original result is replayed once the first attempt finished, and a retry while it is still running is rejected with 409 rather than starting a second send. A key reused for a different message is rejected with 409 too, so pick a new one per send. Keys are scoped to your app and the sending creator, and are remembered for 24 hours.

MessageValidationError.description: Message validation failed (media ownership, content validation, etc.)

AgencyInviteError.description: An agency invite was refused. The value identifies which precondition failed: USER_NOT_ALLOWED (the address is banned, belongs to a creator account, or the caller does not hold team-management permission in the agency being invited into), invitation-already-sent (this address already holds a seat or pending invite in this agency), team-member-already-agency-manager (this address already manages another agency), team-member-account-not-found (no Fanvue account exists for this address — the invitee has to sign up first).

PerKeyError.description: Per-key error returned inside a batch endpoint's 200 response when an individual key cannot be resolved: forbidden (scope doesn't grant access to this key), not_found (key doesn't exist), or internal (server failure on this key only). Batches keep partial results instead of failing the whole request.

EarningSource.description:
What produced this earning.

`renewal` is a catch-all for every recurring charge after the first payment: profile subscriptions, checkout-link subscriptions and fan-experience subscriptions all bill as `renewal` from their second charge onwards. So `subscription`, `checkoutLink` and `fanExperience` only ever hold first payments and one-off purchases. `appStore` is the single exception: an app's recurring charges stay `appStore`.

`fanExperience` and `appStore` are different sides of a third-party app: `fanExperience` is the creator selling a paid experience to a fan, `appStore` is the app's developer selling to the creator, so an `appStore` row is not fan-to-creator spend. `referral`, `affiliate` and `giveaway` are creator rewards rather than fan purchases. `user` follows the invoice rather than the source: it is null when the row records no fan, the common case for those three, and a `giveaway` granted to a specific fan returns that fan.

Reversals are surfaced here too: `refund` and `chargeback` rows carry negative gross/net, matching /insights/spending. A reversal reports the source the creator sees on it in their own earnings: `chargeback` for a bank dispute and for a refund Fanvue issued to stop one (the fan's bank flagged the payment as fraud or raised a dispute alert), `refund` for every other refund and for a payment cancelled before it was collected. Filtering by `source` follows the same split.

`earningsDeduction` is Fanvue taking back the creator's earnings from a sale without refunding the fan, for example when the content sold is removed by moderation. Referral and affiliate rewards from that sale are taken back the same way. The row carries a negative `net`. If the sale is later refunded or charged back, the deduction is released with a second `earningsDeduction` row carrying the matching positive `net`, so the refund or chargeback row does not take the same earnings twice.

SpendingSource.description: A reversal reports the source the creator sees on it in their own earnings: `chargeback` for a bank dispute and for a refund Fanvue issued to stop one (the fan's bank flagged the payment as fraud or raised a dispute alert), `refund` for every other refund and for a payment cancelled before it was collected. Filtering by `source` follows the same split.

error.description: `fan_experiences_not_enabled`: the creator is outside the fan-experiences rollout. `app_not_installed`: the creator has not installed your app. `app_not_available`: your app is not approved, suspended or archived, so it cannot carry experiences. `experience_suspended`: Fanvue removed this experience for a policy reason; it refuses writes until Fanvue reinstates it.
